biggest_catch: No annual fee, so the math is simple and modest: 10,000 SkyMiles (worth roughly $120 at ~1.2 cents each) for $1,000 of planned spending in six months — a straight ~$120 net. Small bonus, but also small ask.
catches: Only claim this bonus if you were ALREADY going to spend $1,000 in six months — never spend extra to chase a bonus.
No annual fee, so the fee doesn't eat the bonus — net is roughly $120 in miles.
This is a modest bonus by design — don't expect it to fund a vacation; 10,000 miles covers a fraction of a domestic award ticket.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry.

Once-per-lifetime rule with a WIDE net: no welcome offer if you have or have had this Card, the Delta SkyMiles Options Credit Card, the Delta Gold, the Delta Platinum, or the Delta Reserve — or previous versions of these cards.
Amex's eligibility check can also deny the welcome offer based on your history (balance transfers, Card Member history, cards opened/closed); you are notified before processing so you can withdraw.
Carrying a balance at ~20%+ APR wipes out the bonus instantly — pay in full.
Fees, interest, cash advances, gift cards, prepaid reloads, and person-to-person payments don't count toward the $1,000 threshold; account must not be cancelled or past due at fulfillment.

steps: Apply for the Delta Blue Card on the official Amex page.
If Amex shows a no-bonus eligibility pop-up during the application, withdraw before the hard inquiry.
If approved, spend $1,000 on eligible purchases you were already planning within the first 6 months of Card Membership.
Pay the balance in full every month.
Keep the account open, not past due; the 10,000 miles post 8-12 weeks after you hit $1,000.
Use the miles toward a Delta award ticket (worth roughly 1.2 cents each).
timing: Bonus miles are credited 8-12 weeks after you meet the $1,000 spend threshold.
